name: Install state without a prompt
plain: A page can tell whether it runs inside an installed app window or a normal tab, with no prompt.
meaning: The display-mode media queries, navigator.standalone on iPhone and the appinstalled event reveal whether you installed the site, stable across visits.

chrome.note: standalone, minimal-ui, fullscreen, browser and window-controls-overlay queries all work

safari.note: display-mode works; appinstalled and beforeinstallprompt do not exist

firefox.note: display-mode queries work, but there is no install, so only browser mode ever matches

ios_safari.note: display-mode works for Home Screen apps; navigator.standalone is the older iOS check

data.metric: A page can tell whether it runs inside an installed app window or a normal tab, with no prompt.

fields.name: display-mode
fields.range: browser, minimal-ui, standalone, fullscreen, window-controls-overlay, tabbed, picture-in-picture

limits.headline: Can tell if you installed the site as an app, and nothing asks you
limits.user_action: None, the page reads it silently
can: Read the window mode with a media query
Learn on iPhone whether the page was opened from the Home Screen
Hear about a fresh install on Chromium
cannot: Tell which other sites you installed
Show anything to you, there is no prompt to refuse
Trigger an install on iPhone, where beforeinstallprompt does not exist
limits.reach_label: One yes or no per visit
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge also fire appinstalled. Safari and iPhone have no beforeinstallprompt, so a site can only read the mode, not offer to install.

story.what_it_is: The page can tell whether it is open in an installed app window, a tab or fullscreen.

marketing.name: display-mode media feature
marketing.pitch: Lets a site tell whether it runs in a browser tab or as an installed app.

story.for_you: Nothing appears on screen. A site simply knows whether you are using its installed app, and can switch layouts or hide its install banner.
story.for_makers: Makers hide install banners for people who already installed, and measure how many visits come from installed windows.

use_cases.example: A web editor hides its install button once it runs standalone.
A news site counts installed app sessions apart from browser visits.

risks: Reveals install status with no prompt
Stable between visits, so it adds to a fingerprint
story.ios_note: On iPhone, navigator.standalone and the display-mode query are the only signals. There is no install event.

technical_bounds: Safari and iOS have no beforeinstallprompt or appinstalled
Firefox on computers has no install, so only browser mode matches
fullscreen mode is partial in Safari, Firefox and Chrome Android per the compat data

abuse: Tell installed users from others for targeting

history.change: Safari 17 adds Add to Dock, display-mode works for those apps
